meta.title: murmur · your site answers its visitors
meta.description: An AI chat bubble that answers from your own pages and links to them. One script tag, no backend, any model through llm-connect. Free and open source.
nav.label: Main
board.title: Your site answers its visitors.
board.lede: murmur adds a chat bubble that answers from your own pages, cites them and links to the right heading. One script tag, no backend, the AI model you pick.
board.q1: How do I add it to my site?
board.q2: Where is my API key stored?
board.q3: Does it work on GitHub Pages?
board.note: This demo has no key of its own: run a small model in your browser (WebGPU, about 1.1 GB once), bring your key (it stays encrypted in your browser) or point it at Ollama on your machine.
board.greeting: Ask me anything about murmur. I answer from the pages of this site and link to them.
field.strip: Every jack is a section of this site; cited ones light up.
field.none: No line answers that question on this site.
field.error: Line dropped: see the message in the chat.
snippet.label: One line
wire.title: Set it up, copy one line.
wire.intro: Pick who holds the AI key, write a greeting, choose a colour. The snippet updates as you go; paste it before </body> on every page.
wire.modeVisitorHint: No download: each visitor pastes their own key once.
wire.modeProxyHint: Most sites: visitors just chat, your key stays secret in a tiny Worker.
wire.proxyHint: Any OpenAI-compatible endpoint works. The Cloudflare Worker in the repository is about 40 lines and keeps the key as a secret.
wire.indexHint: Leave empty to answer from the page the visitor is on. For the whole site, run npx murmur-rag index on your build output.
wire.greetingPlaceholder: Hi! Ask me anything about this site.
wire.instructionsPlaceholder: You are the assistant of the Acme bakery. Be warm and brief.
wire.after: Works on any site that can take a script tag: GitHub Pages, Astro, Hugo, WordPress, Webflow, a plain HTML file.
wire.warnEndpoint: The proxy URL must start with https:// (http:// only for localhost).
how.title: From your pages to an answer, without a server.
how.intro: Everything happens in the visitor's browser. Your site only serves static files.
how.s1text: npx murmur-rag index reads your HTML or Markdown and writes murmur-index.json: your pages cut into passages under their headings. No index? The widget reads the page it is on.
how.s2text: The question is matched against the passages with keyword search (BM25): accents, plurals and typos are forgiven. The best few go to the model.
how.s3text: The model writes from those passages only, cites them [1] [2] and links to the heading they come from. If your pages do not say it, it says so.
keys.title: Your AI key never goes in your HTML.
keys.intro: Anything in a web page can be read by anyone. murmur gives you three ways around it.
keys.proxyText: Deploy the example Cloudflare Worker (free tier) with your key as a secret. It only accepts your site's origin, fixes the model and caps each answer. Visitors chat with no setup.
keys.visitorText: From the AI settings, visitors can connect a provider with their own key instead. llm-connect encrypts it in their browser (AES-GCM, a key the page cannot export) and sends it only to that provider. data-local="false" offers only this.
npm.title: Take the whole thing, or one layer.
npm.intro: murmur-rag is one package with separate entry points. Use the bubble as is, or only the retrieval, or your own model and UI.
npm.root: createMurmur: ask a question, get a streamed answer and its sources. No UI.
npm.rag: Chunking, BM25 retriever, prompt grounding, citations. Bring your own Retriever for embeddings.
npm.indexer: Index HTML, Markdown or text, in Node or in the browser.
npm.llm: The llm-connect wiring: proxy settings, the visitor's settings store.
npm.widget: The <murmur-chat> element, mountMurmur(), the Markdown renderer.
npm.cli: Index a build folder, a set of files or a live sitemap.xml.
npm.c1: install, then index your build output
npm.c2: the bubble, from your own bundle
npm.c3: or headless, with any AI SDK model
npm.c3q: What does the Pro plan include?
limits.title: What it does not do.
limits.l1text: BM25 finds passages that share words with the question. Synonyms it has never seen can miss; plug in your own retriever for semantic search.
limits.l2text: The index downloads with the first question. A few hundred pages is fine; tens of thousands deserve a search service.
limits.l3text: In visitor-key mode the browser calls the provider directly: OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Mistral, OpenRouter, Groq and local servers do; some providers refuse.
limits.l4: Answers are as good as the model
limits.l4text: Grounding and citations cut down invented answers, they do not end them. Check what the bubble says about prices or legal matters.
play.title: Chat with any text.
play.intro: Paste text, Markdown or HTML, or drop files. murmur indexes them in this tab and you can ask about them right away. Nothing is uploaded except the passages sent to your AI provider.
play.placeholder: Paste a page, a README, notes, an FAQ…
play.empty: Index something on the left, then ask about it here.
play.greeting: Indexed. What do you want to know?
play.nothing: Nothing to index yet: paste some text or add a file.
wire.modeLocalHint: No key, no server: a 1.1 GB model runs on the visitor's GPU.
wire.localHint: LFM3 1.7B by Liquid AI downloads once (about 1.1 GB) and stays in the browser's cache; murmur asks the browser to keep it, and a model already cached is prepared in the background on the next visit. Slower and less precise than a hosted model.
keys.localTitle: No key at all, by default
keys.localText: Without a proxy, the visitor's browser runs LFM3 1.7B (Liquid AI, October 2026) on WebGPU. About 1.1 GB downloads once, after the visitor agrees; then questions never leave the device. Slower and less precise than a hosted model.
limits.l5text: LFM3 1.7B needs WebGPU (recent Chrome, Edge, Safari) and about 1.1 GB on first use. It answers in seconds once loaded, with less nuance than a hosted model.
wire.modeAutoHint: The browser model, and visitors may connect their own key instead.
wire.modeOwnerHint: Visitors just chat with your key, which anyone can read.
wire.preloadIdle: As soon as the page is idle
wire.ownerWarn: This key will be in your HTML: anyone can read and reuse it. Only use a key with a spending limit (OpenRouter, a restricted project key), or a Worker.
